subject.title: [Feature]: TUI: vi/vim keybinding mode for input editor

question: Should OpenClaw implement TUI vi/vim modal editing in its `CustomEditor` wrapper now, or wait for first-class `Editor` support in `@earendil-works/pi-tui` before adding a public OpenClaw config option?
rationale: The requested behavior is a new editing mode plus likely config surface, and the closed companion PR concluded that expected vi behavior belongs at the underlying editor component rather than an OpenClaw-local partial parser.

options.title: Wait for pi-tui support
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/API decision and accept an OpenClaw patch only after `pi-tui` exposes a first-class vi-mode editor option.

options.title: Approve OpenClaw wrapper
options.body: Allow a bounded OpenClaw `CustomEditor` implementation with an explicit reduced vi subset and default-off config, accepting the maintenance burden.

recommendation.title: Wait for pi-tui support
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/API decision and accept an OpenClaw patch only after `pi-tui` exposes a first-class vi-mode editor option.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available TUI/editor ownership signal from current blame, original TUI kit history, and pi-tui API alignment commits.
